thread:
incident-bot: Pager — HIGH — multiple 504/502s reported from inference-gateway (inference-gw-us-west1) for traffic originating in Private VPCs. Thresholds crossed: 5min error rate 18%. Paging oncall.

alex_oncall: I'm on it. I'm seeing 504s from synthetic checks and customer alerts (Mosaic Health). Curl to private route returns 504 quickly.

alex_oncall: quick test:
```
curl -v --resolve inference.internal:443:10.0.4.12 https://inference.internal/api/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x'
* Connected to inference.internal (10.0.4.12) port 443
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
```

maya_sre: same. Observability: spike in 5xx across private routes only. Hosted/public customers unaffected. Suggests egress/peering/NAT path.

raj_neteng: on call for net-eng, joining. Any recent peering/SG changes deployed into us-west1 in last 2 hours?

liz_prodops: we rolled a small egress firewall regex tweak at 09:20 (us-west1) for a customer rollout. Change record: ENG-7921. Could that touch SNAT/peering? It was supposed to be SG-only but I'm checking.

alex_oncall: flow logs show a huge increase in SYN retransmits to external model-hosts from a single private CIDR (10.12.0.0/16). Net metric: ephemeral port utilization on the peering appliance is at 98%.

raj_neteng: that smells like ephemeral port exhaustion / SNAT table churn. Can you paste conntrack stats from the edge NAT host?

maya_sre: grabbing logs. On the gateway appliance (transit-nat-01):
```
# conntrack -S
cpu-0 found 152k entries
entries = 152384

# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
152384
```

raj_neteng: what's nf_conntrack_max? 

maya_sre:
```
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
131072
```

maya_sre: interesting — count > max. That will cause new connections to be dropped (and likely 504s).

alex_oncall: that explains it — conntrack overflow causing packets to be dropped / gateway failing to create SNAT entries.

raj_neteng: Immediate mitigation: increase conntrack_max and reduce timeout for ESTABLISHED short-lived flows. I'll push a knob on the transit NAT appliance.

raj_neteng: running:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=60
```

deploy-bot: applied kernel params on transit-nat-01, transit-nat-02. Params persisted to /etc/sysctl.d/90-conntrack.conf

maya_sre: conntrack_count dropping below threshold now. metrics show error rate falling back to baseline within ~90s.

alex_oncall: can we confirm customer impact and scope? John from CSM on the line.

john_csm: Mosaic Health reports ~35% of inference requests returned 504 between 09:22-09:38 in us-west region. They routed some traffic to backup region and saw success there.

liz_prodops: we should fail traffic to us-west2 fallback for affected customers while we stabilize.

raj_neteng: I've also started tcpdump to verify SYN retries and state creation on transit-nat-01:
```
tcpdump -nni eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0' -c 200
```

raj_neteng: saw lots of SYNs from many short-lived clients consuming ephemeral ports due to client-side aggressive reconnects after early timeouts.

maya_sre: any recent client-side changes? Could be a rollout from Mosaic Health or partner side.

john_csm: Mosaic did a frontend deploy that increased parallel requests per host. We're coordinating rollback but need platform mitigations too.

alex_oncall: timeline so far: 09:18 detect small error blip → 09:20 firewall tweak rolled (low risk) → 09:22 alerts escalate → 09:27 conntrack overflow detected → 09:29 conntrack knobs increased → 09:31 errors drop. Customer impact window ~09:22-09:31 for most traffic, some residual till 09:38.

liz_prodops: immediate action: route affected customers to us-west2 fallback for 1 hour, mark dedicated clusters in us-west1 as throttled in console.

raj_neteng: long-term mitigations I'll own:
- increase conntrack_max baseline on NAT appliances 256k
- add alert when conntrack_count > 70% of max
- tune ephemeral port range and reduce client reconnect storms with token bucket policing on transit path

maya_sre: SRE actions:
- add a dashboard cell for conntrack usage per-nat
- add runbook steps for conntrack overflow (sysctl bump + graceful failover)

alex_oncall: customer comms: John, please send Mosaic Health a summary and apology; offer a 24-hr SLA credit option if they want it.

john_csm: will do. Sending initial note now.

deploy-bot: rollback of ENG-7921 firewall tweak approved and staged to us-west1. Rolling in 5m.

alex_oncall: after rollback and conntrack knob we've seen stable metrics. Marking incident as mitigated. Moving to handoff for post-incident follow-up.

raj_neteng: taking postmortem. I'll own RCA and action items. Preliminary root cause: client-side concurrency spike + insufficient conntrack sizing on transit NAT -> SNAT entry eviction -> connection failures -> client retry storm amplifies load.

maya_sre: opening follow-up ticket SRE-4107 with checklist and runbook updates. I'll include the tcpdump/snippets and graph links.

alex_oncall: final notes: no data breach, no model corruption. Impacted customers: Mosaic Health (noted), 3 other private tenants with decreased throughput (non-critical). Total mitigation time ~13 minutes to major mitigation, residual clearing by 09:38.

john_csm: sent customer note and will follow up with compensation options.

raj_neteng: postmortem owner: raj_neteng

alex_oncall: thanks everyone for quick triage. Closing notification thread — follow-ups in SRE-4107 and ENG-7921 rollback thread.
